{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015NqYyPswqXbHL9YFgEszXE","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport { readFileSync } from 'fs';\n2\timport { basename, join, relative } from 'path';\n3\timport { execFileSync } from 'child_process';\n4\t\n5\timport { MODULE_SCHEMAS } from '../../libs/backend-common/src/database/schema-manager.service';\n6\timport { stripComments } from './helpers/ts-source';\n7\t\n8\t/**\n9\t * Tenant provisioning is migration REPLAY: the orchestrator pins\n10\t * `search_path` to `tenant_<uuid>` and runs each tenant-aware service's\n11\t * migration set. Anything that\n12\t * names its schema explicitly — or re-pins the session to the source schema —\n13\t * escapes it, lands in the source schema, and is STILL recorded in the tenant's\n14\t * ledger as applied. This spec is the gate for that class.\n15\t *\n16\t * ## Why this spec was rewritten (DATA-HIGH-012)\n17\t *\n18\t * The previous detector was a single regex looking for a DDL keyword followed\n19\t * by a `\"<source schema>\".` identifier, plus a filename allowlist and a blanket\n20\t * exclusion for every Baseline. It enumerated one SPELLING of the defect rather\n21\t * than testing the property, and both halves of that leaked:\n22\t *\n23\t *   - MSG-HIGH-077 shipped a per-tenant migration that re-pinned its own source\n24\t *     schema — functionally identical to qualifying every statement in the file\n25\t *     — CITING THIS GUARD in its docblock as evidence of its own correctness.\n26\t *   - DATA-CRITICAL-010 (no new tenant can be provisioned) lived entirely\n27\t *     inside the Baseline exclusion.\n28\t *\n29\t * It now asks the actual question — *does this migration issue DDL against a\n30\t * PER-TENANT table in the source schema, by either spelling?* — using\n31\t * `MODULE_SCHEMAS` as the classifier. Two consumers of one SSoT, not two SSoTs.\n37\t *\n38\t * ## Fail-closed\n39\t *\n40\t * A qualified identifier the registry cannot explain is a VIOLATION, not a\n41\t * pass. An unregistered per-tenant table is exactly the shape that would\n42\t * otherwise slip through, so \"I don't recognise this\" resolves against the\n43\t * migration and lands in the reviewer allowlist below with a written reason.\n44\t */\n45\t\n46\tconst REPO_ROOT = join(__dirname, '..', '..');\n47\t\n48\t/** Source schema per tenant-aware migration directory. */\n49\tconst TENANT_AWARE_MIGRATION_DIRS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = [\n50\t  ['apps/farm-service/src/database/migrations', 'farm'],\n51\t  ['apps/sensor-service/src/database/migrations', 'sensor'],\n52\t  ['apps/hr-service/src/database/migrations', 'hr'],\n53\t  ['apps/messaging-service/src/migrations', 'messaging'],\n54\t  ['apps/messaging-service/src/database/migrations', 'messaging'],\n55\t  ['apps/alert-engine/src/database/migrations', 'alert'],\n56\t  ['apps/ai-service/src/database/migrations', 'ai'],\n57\t  ['apps/hydroponics-service/src/database/migrations', 'hydroponics'],\n58\t];\n59\t\n60\t/** A DDL verb + object immediately preceding a qualified identifier. */\n61\tconst DDL_LEAD =\n62\t  /\\b(?:CREATE|ALTER|DROP|TRUNCATE)\\s+(?:UNIQUE\\s+)?(?:TABLE|INDEX|TYPE|SEQUENCE|VIEW|MATERIALIZED\\s+VIEW)\\b(?:\\s+IF\\s+(?:NOT\\s+)?EXISTS)?[\\s\\S]{0,220}$/i;\n63\t\n64\t/**\n65\t * Tables that exist in a shipped migration's DDL but in NEITHER\n66\t * `MODULE_SCHEMAS[].tables` nor `[].infrastructureTables`, because a later\n67\t * migration retired them. They cannot be classified and they cannot be edited\n68\t * out of an immutable migration, so they are named here with the migration that\n69\t * retired them. Not a\n100\t  // per-tenant table wrongly schema-qualified — the fan-out lands it everywhere.\n101\t  '1808000000000-AddVfdDeviceEdgeBinding.ts',\n102\t  // SEC-MEDIUM-083: partial unique index on the per-tenant vfd_change_sets\n103\t  // table — canonical `sensor` copy + tenant fan-out (same pattern as\n104\t  // 1808000000000 above).
